exposure: Maternal risk factors (amniotic fluid volume, length of pPPROM period, completing antibiotherapy, CRP values, chorioamnionitis, placental abruption)

Neonatal risk factors (gestational age at pPPROM, gestational age at birth, new-born weight at birth, 1st and 5th minute Apgar scores, umbilical cord pH value, need for neonatal resuscitation, respiratory distress syndrome, necrotising enterocolitis, intraventricular haemorrhage, retinopathy of prematurity)
outcome: Neonatal complications (respiratory distress syndrome, necrotising enterocolitis, intraventricular haemorrhage, retinopathy of prematurity)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 192 pregnancies complicated by previable premature rupture of membranes (pPPROM) between 14 and 24 weeks gestation.
finding: Gestational age at birth, newborn weight at birth, the presence of oligo-anhydramnios, and the latency period from pPPROM to delivery were significant determinants of neonatal survival and complication rates.
followup_time: until the end of the neonatal period (up to 28 days post-birth)
birth_weight: N/A (new-born weight at birth was measured as a risk factor, but specific weights of the cohort are not provided)
gest_age: pPPROM occurred between 14 and 24 weeks; mean gestational age at pPPROM was 20.45 weeks.
